chunks: As for what al-Saffar narrated from Ibrahim ibn Hashim, from Nuh ibn Shu'ayb, from one who narrated it, from 'Ubayd ibn Zurarah, who said:

I said to him: Is ghusl required upon a woman from her janabah if a man has not come to her? He said: No. And which of you would be pleased to see, or endure that, to see his daughter, or his sister, or his mother, or his wife, or one of his female relatives standing to perform ghusl, and then he says: What is the matter with you? And she says: I had a wet dream, while she has no husband.
Then he said: No, that is not upon them, and Allah has imposed that upon you.
Allah, the Exalted, said: “And if you are in a state of janabah, then purify yourselves.”

And He did not say that concerning them. So this is a mursal report which cannot be used to oppose what we have previously presented of the reports. And it is possible that the intended meaning in it is what we said regarding the first report equally, and that further clarifies it.

key_terms.جَنَابَتِهَا: her state of janabah, major ritual impurity
key_terms.خَبَرٌ مُرْسَلٌ: a report with a disconnected chain
key_terms.غُسْلٌ: ritual bath required in certain states of ritual impurity

ai.seo_question: Is ghusl obligatory for a woman if she experiences janabah without intercourse?
ai.summary: This report discusses whether ghusl is obligatory upon a woman due to janabah when there has been no intercourse. The closing analysis states that this report is mursal and cannot override the previously cited narrations, while also suggesting a reconciliatory interpretation. It also cites the Qur'anic phrase regarding purification from janabah in support of the discussion.
